title: Split etale pull-push counit for quasi-coherent modules
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X,Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact separated etale morphism, with quasi-compactness and separatedness as in [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] on the small etale structure sheaves and the canonical tensor pullback/direct image adjunction $f^*\dashv f_*$ of [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$ [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], its adjunction counit $\epsilon_F:f^*f_*F\to F$ admits an $\mathcal O_X$-linear section: there is a module morphism $s_F:F\to f^*f_*F$ with $\epsilon_F\circ s_F=\operatorname{id}_F$. In particular $F$ is a retract of $f^*f_*F$. No finiteness or Noetherian hypothesis on the spaces or on $F$ is imposed.

proof.text: Put $W=X\times_YX$, with $p$ the first projection and $q$ the second. Apply [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction] to the square with bottom map $f:X\to Y$. Since $f$ is etale, it gives a natural $\mathcal O_X$-linear isomorphism $\beta:f^*f_*F\simeq q_*p^*F$. More concretely, on an etale scheme $u:T\to X$, let $T_Y$ denote $T\xrightarrow{u}X\xrightarrow{f}Y$ and $W_T=X\times_YT$. The same node identifies $(f^*f_*F)(T)=(f_*F)(T_Y)$ with compatible sections of $F$ on the etale scheme charts of $W_T$, or equivalently sections of $p^*F$ over $W_T$. These are compatible with restriction in $T$. Fibre products and their etale projections exist by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]; sections on space objects and sheaf gluing there are justified by [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. We use the actual restriction comparison, not an unspecified isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 03LX (lemma-pushforward-etale-base-change-modules), 03LV (lemma-etale-exact-pullback), 03LW (equation-restrict-modules), 03G1 (lemma-compare-etale-sites); Tag 0HAP first sentence, with the affine-base-change reference corrected to etale base change.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-separated-etale-diagonal-complement], $\Delta:X\to W$ is open and closed. Let $C$ be its open and closed complement. Pulling this partition back along $W_T\to W$, $(x,t)\mapsto(x,u(t))$, gives a partition $W_T=D_T\amalg C_T$. Its first part is the graph $d_T:T\to W_T$, $t\mapsto(u(t),t)$: on every test scheme the equation defining the pullback is exactly $x=u(t)$. Thus $D_T\simeq T$ and $p\circ d_T=u$, whereas the second projection composed with $d_T$ is $\operatorname{id}_T$. On every scheme chart the two parts are complementary open subsets, so they give a disjoint open cover without any finiteness hypothesis on $T$ or on the spaces.

source.place: Tag 0HAP (lemma-etale-pull-push-split), open and closed diagonal; openness also spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 05W1 (lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism), part (1).

proof.text: For $t\in F(T)$ define $a_T(t)$ as follows. On $D_T\simeq T$ take $t$, using $p\circ d_T=u$ and the etale restriction identification of step 1; on $C_T$ take zero. These sections glue uniquely: on each etale scheme chart $E\to W_T$ restrict $t$ to the open part $E\times_{W_T}D_T$, and use zero on $E\times_{W_T}C_T$; their intersection is empty, so the sheaf axiom gives a unique section on $E$. Uniqueness makes these sections compatible on all chart maps. This constructs the compatible family $a_T(t)$ appearing in step 1 using only the sheaf axiom for [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. No claim about quasi-coherence of a complementary summand is needed.

source.place: Tag 0HAP, direct-summand construction, written sectionwise using sites-modules.tex Tag 03CV (definition-sheaf-modules).

proof.text: The maps $a_T$ are linear for $\mathcal O_X(T)$ acting through the second projection $W_T\to T$: on $D_T$ that projection is the identity and the scalar action is the usual action on $t$, while on $C_T$ every scalar kills zero. Sums and scalar multiples of the glued sections therefore have the prescribed restrictions and equal the corresponding glued section by uniqueness. For a map $T'\to T$ over $X$, the inverse image of $D_T$ is $D_{T'}$ (the equation $x=u(t)$ pulls back to the same equation for $T'$), and likewise for the complement. Restricting $a_T(t)$ consequently gives $a_{T'}(t|_{T'})$, again by uniqueness. Thus step 1 turns the $a_T$ into an $\mathcal O_X$-module morphism $s_F:F\to f^*f_*F$. This is the definition of a linear sheaf morphism in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tag 0HAP, the inclusion of the diagonal summand; sites-modules.tex Tag 03CV, module morphisms and restrictions.

proof.text:
Identify the given counit, not merely a retraction of the underlying object. For $m\in(f_*F)(T_Y)$ let $\pi_T(m)\in F(T)$ be its chart projection for $(T,\operatorname{id}_{T_Y})$ in [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. This is restriction of the compatible family to $d_T$. Write $B=f_*F$ and $P=f^*$. The adjunction triangle $f_*(\epsilon_F)\circ\eta_B=\operatorname{id}_B$, evaluated at $T_Y$ and then at this chart projection, gives
$$\epsilon_F(T)\bigl(\pi_T(\eta_B(m))\bigr)=\pi_T(m).$$
Here the projection on the left has value in $(PB)(T)$. By the chart-unit tensor formula of [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] and its etale normalization in [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization], this value is $1\otimes m$, which corresponds to $m$ under $(PB)(T)=B(T_Y)$, the restriction identification of [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction]. Thus $\epsilon_F(T)$ is exactly restriction to $D_T$. By construction $a_T(t)|_{D_T}=t$, so $\epsilon_F(T)s_F(T)(t)=t$. This holds for every etale scheme $T\to X$ and every section $t$, hence $\epsilon_F\circ s_F=\operatorname{id}_F$. Empty charts and the zero module obey the same formulas. This proves the claimed retract under all the stated hypotheses.

The statement and stmt_deps are identical to the live copy, which is still unsplit, so no other group has superseded it. Source: Stacks 0HAP. Its proof cites affine base change 07U8, but that lemma needs f affine (the punctured-plane immersion is a counterexample); the delivery correctly uses étale base change 03LX through lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction and reports this under Source error. Step 1: the self-square with g=f gives the section-level identification of f^*f_*F with sections of F over X×_Y T, which the cited node states. Step 2: the clopen-diagonal clause of lem-sfb-space-separated-etale-diagonal-complement applies (f separated and étale); its pullback to X×_Y T is the graph of u. Steps 3 and 4 are genuinely elementary: disjoint two-open gluing, then linearity through q_T with q_T∘d_T=id, and naturality because preimages of graphs are graphs. Step 5: the triangle identity, the chart-unit formula 1⊗m and the étale clause of the tensor realization show that the specified counit is restriction to the graph, so ε∘s=id. This supplies the source's 'details omitted'. Edge cases checked: empty X, f=id, Y⊔Y→Y and infinite disjoint unions. Quasi-coherence and quasi-compactness are unused but kept in the statement, so nothing is weakened. No duplicate: 0HAP occurs only in the item and its one citer; same-unit lem-sfb-space-higher-image-etale-restriction lacks the section formula, and the flat base-change node needs scheme bases. I accept the 4 trf tool_uses as generic foundations of étale modules on algebraic spaces. lean.statement: theorem exists_section_moduleTensorAdjunction_counit {S : Scheme.{u}} {X Y : AlgebraicSpace S} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hfqc : IsQuasiCompactPresheafMap f.hom.hom) (hfsep : IsSeparatedPresheafMap f.hom.hom) (hfet : IsEtale f.hom.hom) (F : X.Modules) [SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent F] : ∃ s : F ⟶ (moduleTensorPullback f).obj ((moduleDirectImage f).obj F), s ≫ (moduleTensorAdjunction f).counit.app F = 𝟙 F
